topics.title: Circuit Analysis
topics.description: Systematic methods for analyzing electrical circuits — node voltage and mesh current methods.
objectives: Apply the node voltage method
Apply the mesh current method
Use superposition and source transformation
Apply Thevenin and Norton equivalent circuits

problem_templates.prompt_template: A circuit has nodes A and B with a 10 V source between ground and A, R₁ = 5Ω (A to B), R₂ = 10Ω (B to ground), R₃ = 20Ω (B to ground). Apply the node voltage method to find V_B and all branch currents.

Find the Thevenin equivalent circuit seen by R_L in a circuit with V_s = 24 V, R₁ = 6Ω in series from the source, R₂ = 12Ω in parallel with the terminals. Compute V_th and R_th. Find I_L when R_L = 8Ω.
Use superposition to find the current through R₃ = 4Ω in a circuit with two sources: V₁ = 12 V and V₂ = 6 V, plus R₁ = 2Ω and R₂ = 3Ω. Analyze with each source active separately, then sum.

topics.title: AC Circuits
topics.description: Analysis of circuits with sinusoidal sources using phasors and impedance.
objectives: Represent sinusoidal signals with phasors
Define impedance for resistors, inductors, and capacitors
Analyze AC circuits in the frequency domain
Compute power in AC circuits

problem_templates.prompt_template: A series RLC circuit has R = 10Ω, L = 50 mH, C = 100 μF driven by v(t) = 20 cos(200t) V. Find the impedance Z, the phasor current, and the actual time-domain current i(t).
Find the resonant frequency, bandwidth, and quality factor Q for a parallel RLC circuit with R = 1 kΩ, L = 10 mH, C = 1 μF. Sketch the impedance magnitude vs. frequency.

In an AC circuit, R = 8Ω, X_L = 6Ω (inductive reactance). Compute the apparent power S, real power P, reactive power Q, and power factor. Describe what capacitance value at ω = 100 rad/s would bring the power factor to unity.

topics.title: Operational Amplifiers
topics.description: The ideal op-amp model and common configurations — inverting, non-inverting, summing, integrator.
objectives: Apply the ideal op-amp rules
Analyze inverting and non-inverting amplifier circuits
Design summing amplifiers and integrators
Understand feedback and stability qualitatively

problem_templates.prompt_template: An inverting amplifier has R_f = 100 kΩ and R_in = 10 kΩ. Find the voltage gain. If v_in = 0.5 sin(1000t) V, find v_out. State the two ideal op-amp rules used.
Design a summing amplifier to compute v_out = −(2v₁ + 3v₂). Choose R_f = 60 kΩ and find R₁ and R₂. Verify your design by computing v_out for v₁ = 1 V, v₂ = 0.5 V.

An op-amp integrator has R = 10 kΩ, C = 1 μF. If v_in = 2 V (constant), find v_out(t) starting from 0 V. At what time does |v_out| reach 10 V (the supply rail)? Explain what happens to ideal vs. real integrators at DC.

topics.title: Digital Logic
topics.description: Boolean algebra, logic gates, combinational and sequential logic circuits.
objectives: Apply Boolean algebra and De Morgan's theorems
Design and simplify combinational logic circuits
Build flip-flops and sequential logic
Understand binary number representation

problem_templates.prompt_template: Simplify the Boolean expression F = AB + A'C + BC using Boolean algebra laws. Verify with a truth table. Implement using only NAND gates.
Design a 2-bit binary adder. Write the truth table for sum and carry outputs, derive the minimal SOP expressions, and draw the logic gate schematic.

Design a D flip-flop-based 2-bit synchronous up-counter. Draw the state diagram, write the state transition table, derive the D inputs, and describe the output sequence for 4 clock cycles starting from 00.

topics.title: Signal Processing
topics.description: Fourier analysis, filtering, and the frequency-domain view of signals.
objectives: Compute Fourier series for periodic signals
Apply the Fourier transform and understand its properties
Design simple low-pass and high-pass filters
Introduce discrete-time signals and the DFT

problem_templates.prompt_template: Find the Fourier series of a square wave with amplitude A and period T. Compute the DC term and the first three non-zero harmonics. Sketch the partial sum through the 5th harmonic.
A first-order RC low-pass filter has R = 1 kΩ and C = 1 μF. Find the cutoff frequency f_c. Plot |H(jω)| in dB at 0.1f_c, f_c, and 10f_c. Describe the phase response.
A signal x[n] = {1, 2, 3, 4} (N=4). Compute the 4-point DFT X[k] for k = 0, 1, 2, 3 using the DFT formula X[k] = Σ x[n]·e^(−j2πkn/N). Identify the DC component and the Nyquist component.
